standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of regular sections of the structure sheaf, which reduces the existence of pullbacks of meromorphic functions to the requirement that the ring map send nonzerodivisors to nonzerodivisors
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the sheaf-theoretic statement into the algebraic statement about nonzerodivisors.

standard_prerequisites.name: An element is a nonzerodivisor exactly when it lies outside every weakly associated prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the main case, where the hypothesis on weakly associated points prevents the image of a nonzerodivisor from being a zerodivisor.

standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison between associated and weakly associated primes, and the description of weakly associated points of a reduced scheme, both cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Derives the locally Noetherian cases and the reduced case from the main case.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elements of a minimal prime of a ring are zerodivisors
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that a nonzerodivisor avoids every minimal prime, which is what the hypotheses on the images of the relevant points supply.

core_obligations: Reduce to algebra: the question is local, so assume affine source and target with a ring map between the coordinate rings, and by the criterion for regular sections it suffices to prove that the ring map sends nonzerodivisors to nonzerodivisors (proof lines 6006-6012).
Flat case: if the ring map is flat then injectivity of multiplication by a nonzerodivisor on the target ring implies injectivity on the source ring, which gives the last case (proof lines 6014-6016).

Main case: a nonzerodivisor lies outside every minimal prime because elements of minimal primes are zerodivisors, so under the hypothesis that every weakly associated point of the source maps to a generic point of the target the image of the element avoids every weakly associated prime of the source, hence is a nonzerodivisor (proof lines 6014-6020).

Specializations: the locally Noetherian cases follow from the main case using the comparison between associated and weakly associated primes and the definitions, and the reduced case follows from the main case using the description of weakly associated points of a reduced scheme, with the integral and dominant cases being special cases of the reduced one (proof lines 6021-6031).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a ring map and to the requirement that nonzerodivisors be preserved (proof lines 6006-6012).
Handle flatness directly and the remaining cases by showing that a nonzerodivisor avoids the weakly associated primes of the source, then specialize (proof lines 6014-6031).
difficulty_reason: The lemma lists seven geometric situations in which pullbacks of meromorphic functions along a morphism are defined, ranging from flat morphisms to hypotheses on where weakly associated or associated points are sent (statement lines 5983-6004). The counted proof is a clean reduction: it localizes to a ring map and, by the criterion for regular sections, reduces to showing that nonzerodivisors are preserved; it disposes of the flat case directly by injectivity of multiplication, proves the main case by observing that a nonzerodivisor avoids all minimal primes so that the hypothesis on weakly associated points makes its image a nonzerodivisor, and then specializes to the remaining cases using the comparison between associated and weakly associated primes and the description of weakly associated points of reduced schemes (proof lines 6006-6031). It is H2: every case is derived in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard prime-theoretic facts.
